newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: PHILIPPINE STOCKS - factors to watch - June 20.
newsitem.headline: PHILIPPINE STOCKS - factors to watch - June 20.

text.p: Following are views on the direction of Philippine stocks on Friday and main factors likely to affect trading:
* Investors are likely to cash in on gains after a 100-point run-up in just two days and ahead of the weekend, traders said.

* Market will move sideways with a downward bias as trading may be negatively affected by the Thai baht scare that prompted the Central Bank to raise overnight rates on Thursday, Anscor-Hagedorn Securities analyst Elline Salvatierra said.
* On Thursday, the Philippine composite index closed 82.62 points higher at 2,905.97 points.
* The Dow Jones on Thursday ended 58.35 points higher at 7,777.06. PLDT's ADR closed $0 1/2 lower at $63.
* The Philippine peso closed up at 26.372 to the dollar vs 26.379.
* The Philippine interbank call loan average fell to 12.8125 percent vs 13.0625.
* On Friday, the Central Bank raised its overnight lending rate to 17 percent from 14.75 percent.
* Philippine authorities on Thursday reacted with alarm to a possible fallout of Thailand's woes on the peso and moved quickly to raise interest rates, the second time they have done so in a month.

* The Central Bank had cut its overnight rates Thursday morning by 0.25 percentage point to 14.75 percent. But within hours the lending rate was restored to 15 percent as news came in that the Thai baht was under pressure following the resignation of Thai Finance Minister Amnuray Viravan.

* Pilipinas Shell Petroleum Corp said it will lower prices of liquefied petroleum gasoline and diesel but will keep prices of other petroleum products unchanged. Effective Friday, Shell's diesel prices will be cut by five centavos per litre to 7.65 pesos while its LPG prices will be reduced by two pesos per 11-kg cyliner to 155 pesos.

* The Philippine may post a lower budget surplus of 7.1 billion pesos this year, almost half of the 13 billion-peso surplus it targeted for the year, according to documents from the Development Budget Coordination Committee.
* The Philippines has launched a $500 million Yankee bond in two tranches, one $400 million 30-year tranche and a $100 million 100-year tranche, lead manager Salomon Brothers said.
* BusinessWorld said the National Telecommunications Commission controversial application to install and operate telephone lines nationwide will finally de decided next week.
* Newspapers Inquirer and Today said the Land Bank of the Philippines foreclosed properties of a Victorias Milling Corp subsidiary for failure to pay a 465.62-million loan.
